given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Two loans lent on 03-02 are due on 03-16, and the clock is set to 03-17, so both are open and overdue.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The reminders table starts empty, so no reminder exists for either loan when the job runs.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: `fakeNotifications.sent` must equal exactly two entries, each with the right memberId, loanId and dueOn, so a skipped call or wrong member fails.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: The reminders table rows are asserted as `{loan_id, sent_on: '2026-03-17'}`, with the length checked. A missing row or the wrong date fails.
B3's test shows a refused loan is not recorded, which is the only way a wrong order would show.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice, so loan1 has a reminder from the first run. `sent` must still hold only one entry afterwards.
loan2 would be overdue, but it is returned before the job runs.
member-3's loan is lent on 03-03, so it is due on 03-17, which is today. That tests the boundary where `dueOn` is not before today.

then.why: `toMatchObject` on an array also requires the same length, so `sent` must be exactly `[loan1]`. A send for any of the three excluded loans fails.

given.why: `refuseFor(loan1, ...)` makes the fake return a refused delivery for that loan.
The service test only uses a refusal. B5's test proves a failed connection becomes a refused delivery.
Both loans are overdue, so the job tries to send for each.

then.why: The reminders table must hold exactly one row, for loan2. A row for the refused loan1 fails.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`
then.why: `toContainEqual` matches the exact level, event, loanId and error string, so a change to any of them fails.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan1 is lent first and refused, and loan2 must still be sent. This assumes the job handles loans in lending order.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, one of them refused, and the job runs to completion.

then.why: The last log entry must equal `{level: 'info', event: 'reminders.finished', fields: {sent: 2, failed: 1}}`, so the event name, level, counts and its position as final log are all pinned.

given.why: The tests call `sendOverdueReminder` directly with a reminder fixture.

then.why: The captured request must have method POST, pathname `/notifications` and content-type `application/json`. The client is built with `NOTIFY_URL`.

then.part: body `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: The parsed body is compared with `toEqual` to the exact structure, so a renamed key or a different template fails.
202, 200 and 204 are each accepted, so a check for exactly 200 or exactly 202 would fail.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 gives kind `refused` with a reason containing '400', so a generic reason fails. It also fails if only 5xx counted as refused.

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: A network error gives kind `refused` with a reason containing 'unreachable'.
